verdict.rationale: Runpod documents its own storage controls: network volumes persist data independently of compute, files on them can be managed through an S3-compatible API, and Pods and volumes can be terminated or managed via console, CLI, or API. This gives users practical control over what is kept and what is removed, but nothing in the evidence describes retention policies or deletion guarantees. Missing for 10: explicit data-deletion and retention-policy documentation, guarantees on data wiping after Pod termination or volume deletion, platform-side retention terms for logs and inference data, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Network volumes provide persistent storage that exists independently of your compute resources. Data is retained when terminate or scale to zero.
This allows you to manage files on your network volumes without launching a Pod
Create, start, stop, and terminate Pods using the Runpod console or CLI.
You can manage Pods, Serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, and models
